# CARE plugin docs: questions from first to finish

**One-liner:** One review of three CARE plugin docs, in the order the questions were asked — how plugins load, how host-dev differs from federation, then how a plugin can swap a React component.

**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Context:** Branch `docs/refresh-care-apps-plugin-docs` on `care_fe`. Reading `care-apps-architecture-note.md` → `care-apps-local-dev.md` → `care-apps-override-architecture.md` (+ companion `care-apps-plugin-overrides.md`) against code. Kutumba copied under `apps/` for experiments. Local host experiments (LoginHeader / PrintInvoice / `.env.local`) are **not** production — revert before committing host source.

Denser notes for pieces of this path:

- [`../microfrontends/care-host-dev-plugin-discovery.md`](../microfrontends/care-host-dev-plugin-discovery.md) — why `apps/` exists, Dirent vs symlink, `.ts` vs `.tsx`
- [`../nodejs/dirent-isdirectory-vs-stat.md`](../nodejs/dirent-isdirectory-vs-stat.md)
- [`../javascript/flatmap-to-skip.md`](../javascript/flatmap-to-skip.md)
- [`component-override-register-and-exports.md`](component-override-register-and-exports.md) — sleeve, env allowlist, named vs default (cheat sheet)

---

## 0. Picture to keep in your head

```
CARE host (care_fe)                 Care App (Kutumba, HMIS, …)
───────────────────                 ──────────────────────────
npm run dev                         lives in apps/<slug>/  OR  remoteEntry.js
PluginEngine                        manifest.tsx
  ├─ load plugin                    routes, components, overrides
  ├─ show plugin UI in slots        e.g. PatientRegistrationForm
  └─ addOverride("Foo", plugin)     e.g. swap LoginHeader / PrintInvoice

Override sleeve (register)  ←  page must import THIS, not a second unwrapped export
```

Three docs, three jobs:

| Doc | Job |
|---|---|
| architecture-note | How PluginEngine **picks and loads** plugins |
| local-dev | How `apps/` + Vite make that **cheap on a laptop** |
| override-architecture + plugin-overrides | How a loaded plugin **replaces a host component** |

---

## 1. Architecture note — how plugins get into the app

### What problem does host-dev even solve?

Production path: build the plugin → serve `remoteEntry.js` → `REACT_ENABLED_APPS` → two processes, weak HMR.

Host-dev: drop the plugin under `apps/<slug>/`, one `npm run dev`. Plugin source joins the **same Vite graph**. That is why it is supported — iterate on Kutumba without shipping a federation bundle every save.

**Takeaway:** `apps/` is a **dev shortcut**, not how staging/production load plugins.

### Clone where?

Clone (or copy) **into** `apps/care_kutumba_fe` (a folder with `src/manifest.tsx`). Not a bare dump of files at `apps/` root. Vite looks for `apps/*/src/manifest.tsx`.

A symlink to another checkout **should** work in theory. It did not, until discovery used `stat`/`realpath` instead of `Dirent.isDirectory()` — Node reports a symlink as `isSymbolicLink: true`, `isDirectory: false`, so the folder was skipped. Same empty UI as a missing plugin: **no error banner**.

**Takeaway:** Empty slot → debug **discovery**, not the form. Prefer a real copy under `apps/` unless the symlink fix is on the branch you run.

### Two-stage load (architecture-note)

1. `GET /api/v1/plug_config/` (backend rows).
2. Merge with **build-time** plugins from `getBuildTimePlugConfigs()`.

Build-time has two inputs, both tagged `source: "build"`:

- `REACT_ENABLED_APPS` → `care.config.ts` → `careConfig.careApps` (federation URL). **Every** Vite command (`dev`, `build`, Playwright).
- `apps/*/src/manifest.tsx` → **only** host `npm run dev`.

Same slug in both: **`apps/` wins**. The env remote URL is ignored until you remove the folder.

`org/repo` or `org/repo@host/path/to/remoteEntry.js`. No `@host` → GitHub Pages. `localhost` → `http://`, else `https://`.

### `source: "build"` vs the admin apps page

This was the confusing bit.

Runtime (`PluginEngine`, i18n) uses the **merged** list. Overlap with the API: one entry, `source: "build"`, `isReadOnly: true`, build-time metadata wins, extra API-only keys kept.

`/admin/apps` does **not** use that merge. It lists **only** API rows. Env / `apps/` plugins do not show there. `isReadOnly` is not an admin lock.

Tiny picture:

```
Runtime board:  kutumba { url from apps or env, extra keys from DB }
Admin table:    only rows that exist in plug_config
```

**Takeaway:** “Read-only built-in plugin” is a **runtime** flag, not “you cannot edit `/admin/apps/:slug`.”

### Playwright / `vite build` vs `apps/`

`createLocalPluginModule` is empty unless Vite `command === "serve"`. Playwright’s documented path is `npm run preview` of a **build**. Cloning into `apps/` in CI does **nothing**. Put always-on test plugins in `REACT_ENABLED_APPS` and serve a real remote.

Local exception: if `npm run dev` is already on `:4000` and Playwright `reuseExistingServer` is on (non-CI), tests hit **dev** and `apps/` *does* load. That is not CI.

**Takeaway:** Do not mix “I cloned it under `apps/`” with “Playwright will see it.”

---

## 2. Local-dev — federation, HMR, aliases, clone

### Is local-dev “the Vite federation architecture”?

Only the **production-shaped** half. Host `dev` + `apps/` **skips** federation (`localDevPluginManifests[slug]` → import the in-tree manifest). Federation is: register remote → load `./manifest` from `remoteEntry.js`.

Shared deps (`react`, `react-dom`, `react-i18next`, …) must be **one copy**. Two Reacts → hooks explode. That is why sharing is required, not a style choice.

### Env but not in `/apps`?

Then you are on the federation path. Need a valid `meta.url` and a running remote. Missing/invalid URL → log and skip that plugin; the rest of CARE still loads.

### HMR: get updates without refresh?

**In-tree `apps/`:** yes, normal Vite HMR (same graph).

**Federation remote:** the host does **not** auto-reload when `remoteEntry.js` changes. Refresh the CARE tab. (Doc had overclaimed this.)

### `@` vs `@fs`

- `@` → Vite alias to host `src/` (`@/components/...`).
- `@fs` → Vite serving a **filesystem** path (often after a rewrite fails and it falls back). Not an npm package.

If the plugin import is rewritten to the plugin file, you get the plugin. If rewrite fails, `@/` can silently hit **host** `src/` instead. Sharing / rewrite bugs show up as “wrong module” or invalid hook calls, not a friendly “plugin missing.”

### Clone script: from which directory?

From **care_fe**, and the plugin must be a folder Vite can see under `apps/` (or the script’s documented source). A plugin living only as a remote URL is not cloned by that script.

Binary assets that JS imported (images, fonts, some CSS) are copied; `@import` / `url()` **inside CSS** are not followed. “Every local JS/TS file” in the intro was incomplete — imported assets are copied too; CSS-internal URLs are not.

---

## 3. Override architecture — what the system is

A **notebook** (global `registry` Map): `"LoginHeader"` → original + plugin replacements.

A **sleeve** (`register(key, Base)`): wrapper React component. At render it looks at the notebook and draws Base or a plugin.

**Vite** (`plugins/autoRegisterComponents.ts`) can rewrite `src/**/*.tsx` exports so they call `register()`, but only names on `REACT_MFE_REGISTERED_COMPONENTS`. Empty / unset = wrap **nothing**.

**PluginEngine** reads `overrides: [{ component: "Foo", replacement }]` and calls `addOverride`. Manifest alone is not enough until this runs.

Call sites stay `<Foo />`. They must import the **sleeve**.

```
You write Foo
    │
    ├─ Vite allowlist  →  sleeve on that export (maybe)
    └─ or register() in source →  sleeve always
              │
Page renders sleeve
              │
PluginEngine addOverride("Foo", plugin)
              │
Sleeve looks at notebook → Base or plugin
```

`window.__careOverrides.addComponent` **is** `addOverride`. Federation cannot import `@/lib/override`. Host PluginEngine **can**, and that is the usual path. The window is an escape hatch.

---

## 4. Goal nits we proved with Kutumba

### Sticky note vs board (`userRole`)

`OverrideCondition` can list `page`, `userRole`, `facilityType`, `stackPath`.

The **sticky note** is the plugin: `condition: { userRole: "doctor" }`.
The **board** is `OverrideContext` from `OverrideProvider`.

`App.tsx` is `<OverrideProvider>` with **no** `context` prop. Provider only fills `route` / `page` from the URL. It also sits **above** `AuthUserProvider`, so `user.role` is not even in scope there.

Experiment: unconditional pink `UserDashboard` after staff login → visible. Then `condition: { userRole: "doctor" }` → pink **gone** even as a doctor. `matchValue`: no board value → false.

`page` is not the full URL. First segment (`/facilities` → `"facilities"`). If the second segment looks like an id and a third exists: `/facility/<uuid>/patients` → `"facility-patients"`.

**Takeaway:** A condition key that the board never writes will never match. Unconditional override (no `condition`) always matches.

### Error boundary (experiment C)

Comment in `register.ts` says: throw → render the **base**. Code renders a gray line: *A plugin override for X encountered an error and was replaced with the default.*

Throwing Kutumba `UserDashboard` → **that slot** is the gray line. Sidebar and other routes still work. Not a white screen. Not the original dashboard. Console still says “falling back to base component” — that log is wrong.

Different from PluginEngine’s full-screen *Care has encountered an unexpected error* (plugin load crash).

**Takeaway:** Isolation = that **slot**, not “show the original,” not “crash the app.”

---

## 5. `register()` — you usually don’t type it

Vite rewrite **idea** (actual emit uses `__careRegisterComponent` + `FooRegistered`):

```tsx
const FooRegistered = register("Foo", Foo);
export { FooRegistered as Foo };
```

Docs that show `export default register("Foo", Foo)` are the idea, not the exact AST.

Empty allowlist wraps nothing. Hand-written `register()` is **always-on** (no env). Restart Vite after changing the env list.

Call site must import the **same hole** Vite wrapped (named vs default).

---

## 6. Two export holes (the questions that unlocked PrintInvoice)

A module can ship two values with the same word:

```tsx
export function PrintInvoice() { ... }   // hole 1 — import { PrintInvoice }
export default PrintInvoice;             // hole 2 — import PrintInvoice from
```

`{ PrintInvoice }` is hole 1. `import X from` is hole 2. Same importer word, **two slots**.

`export const LoginHeader = () => …` and `export function LoginHeader() { … }` are both **named** (hole 1). Default is hole 2.

**Why two exports in the first place?** Habit / “works with both import styles.” Not required by React. Most CARE files do **not** do both for the same name (~6 files). Do not assume “CARE always does named + default.” PrintInvoice **did**, and the router only uses default.

**Does the override engine use the default export?** No. The engine uses the **notebook key**. The **page** must render the sleeve. Which export is the sleeve depends on Vite or hand `register()`.

### Why Vite + both doors + default import fails

Vite walks in order:

1. `export function Foo` / `export const Foo` → wrap named, mark `Foo` done.
2. `export default Foo` → **skip** (name already transformed).
3. Default still points at the **original**.

```
named    { Foo }              sleeve
default  import Foo from      original   ← PrintInvoice’s router
```

LoginHeader experiments (`REACT_MFE_REGISTERED_COMPONENTS=LoginHeader`, Kutumba pink):

| File | Page import | Pink? |
|---|---|---|
| `export const` / `export function` only | `{ LoginHeader }` | yes |
| named + `export default LoginHeader` | `import LoginHeader from` | **no** |
| same two doors | `{ LoginHeader }` | yes |
| default-only (`const`/`function` + `export default`) | `import LoginHeader from` | yes |

**Takeaway:** Env wrap works only if the import the page uses is the hole Vite wrapped.

---

## 7. What `export default register("PrintInvoice", PrintInvoiceBase)` means

1. `PrintInvoiceBase` — original UI.
2. `register("PrintInvoice", …)` — notebook key `"PrintInvoice"`, **returns** a sleeve.
3. `export default` — hole 2 **is** that sleeve.

Router `import PrintInvoice from` gets the sleeve. Manifest `component: "PrintInvoice"` matches the key.

This is [care_fe #16441](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/pull/16441) (merged), for HMIS [care_govt_hmis_fe #7](https://github.com/egovhealthcare/care_govt_hmis_fe/pull/7).

### Did they need `PrintInvoiceBase`? (the rename question)

**No**, not for the router. Proved on LoginHeader (pink on `/facilities`):

```tsx
export function LoginHeader() { ... }
export default register("LoginHeader", LoginHeader);
```

Legal JS: function is hoisted; `register(..., LoginHeader)` is the original; default is a **different** value (the sleeve). Named import would be original (or Vite-wrapped named if allowlisted). Default import is the sleeve.

`…Base` only avoids two public values both *called* `PrintInvoice`. Naming habit (same PR first did `InvoiceChargeItemTitleBase`), not a compiler requirement.

Same names **do** work: `export default register("PrintInvoice", PrintInvoice)`.

### Why not just env?

Two ways onto the notebook:

| Way | When it wraps | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Allowlist + Vite | Listed names (or `*`). Empty = nothing | Export name = key; import matches wrapped hole |
| Hand-written `register()` | When the file loads | Put it on the export the call site uses |

Manual `register()` on **default** means: HMIS can override invoice print even if env is empty, **and** hole 2 is the sleeve (router uses default).

Env-only also works if:

- one door matching the import, **or**
- named-only + change router to `{ PrintInvoice }`,

plus `REACT_MFE_REGISTERED_COMPONENTS=PrintInvoice` in **every** deploy that needs it.

Proved on real `PrintInvoice.tsx`: drop default, `export function PrintInvoice`, router `{ PrintInvoice }`, allowlist, Kutumba `__base` wrap → pink **KUTUMBA PRINT** above the invoice.

**So:** manual `register()` on default **did** fix “router must render the sleeve.” The `Base` rename did **not** by itself. Two exports after the PR are fine because they are **different holes**: named `PrintInvoiceBase` = original, default = sleeve.

If there is **only one export** and it matches the import, Vite + env is enough — no hand `register()`, no rename.

Asked on the merged PR: [comment](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/pull/16441#issuecomment-5309057772).

---

## 8. Later override APIs (after `register`)

### `addOverride`

PluginEngine: `addOverride(override.component, { component: override.replacement, … })`.

String `component` = notebook key. `replacement` = the React component that goes in.

Omit `condition` → always match. Sorted by `priority` (highest first), first match wins.

If `register()` has not run yet, addOverride still stores on a **placeholder**. Useless until some sleeve for that key actually renders.

Cleanup: PluginEngine re-runs cleanups when the plugin list changes so stale overrides do not pile up.

### `__base`

Injected only when an override is chosen (`Component !== Base`). Lets the plugin wrap or fall through to the original. Kutumba print used this to keep the real invoice under a banner.

### `stackPath`

Opt-in. Subsequence of the render tree (`PatientCard` under `PatientHome`). Every name in the path must be registered. Fast path skips these entries (`hasStackConditions`). Cost is O(overrides × depth), not O(1).

### Debugging

`getRegisteredKeys()`, `getEntry("Foo")`. Sleeve has `__override_key__`, `__base_component__`, `displayName = Registered(Foo)`.

Vite does **not** rename the original to `FooBase`. DevTools: `Registered(Foo)` wrapping `Foo` (unless you renamed by hand).

---

## Lessons (whole session)

- `apps/` = laptop `npm run dev` only. Production / Playwright preview = `REACT_ENABLED_APPS` and/or `plug_config`.
- Same slug in `apps/` and env: `apps/` wins.
- Admin `/admin/apps` ≠ runtime merge. `source: "build"` is not “hidden from admin.”
- Empty plugin UI: discovery first (symlink Dirent, wrong `manifest.ts` vs `tsx`, slug).
- Sleeve must be what the **call site imports**. Notebook entry alone is not enough.
- Empty allowlist wraps nothing. Manual `register()` is always-on.
- Named + default **same name**: Vite wraps named, skips default. Default import → no override.
- Default-only + default import + env: works (no `Base`).
- `export default register("Foo", Foo)` + default import: works (no `Base`).
- `…Base` is optional naming when keeping a named original plus a default sleeve.
- `condition.userRole` never matches until App fills the board.
- Override crash: gray message in **that slot**; rest of the app lives. Not the original UI.
- Don’t assume “CARE always does named + default.” Count first.

No. **Stack** here is not the URL and not `userRole`.

It means: **who rendered this component in React** — parent → child in the tree.

There are two kinds of conditions:

| Kind | Field | Example | Fast path? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Board (URL / role / facility) | `page`, `route`, `userRole`, `facilityType` | `{ page: "admin" }` | yes — map lookup |
| Stack (render tree) | `stackPath` | `{ stackPath: ["PatientHome", "PatientCard"] }` | no — walk parents |

`stackPath: ["PatientHome", "PatientCard"]` means: only swap `PatientCard` when it is sitting **under** `PatientHome`. Same card on another page/parent → leave it alone.

Tiny picture:

```
PatientHome
  └── PatientCard     ← stack matches → override
SettingsPage
  └── PatientCard     ← same component, different parent → no match
```

That is a **linked list** of `{ name, parent }` built as sleeves render, not `/facility/...` and not doctor vs nurse.

Line 94: if **any** override for this key has `stackPath`, the sleeve cannot use the precomputed map (parents are only known at render). It builds the stack node and checks then.

`page` / `userRole` are **not** stack conditions. They are the other sticky notes on the board.

> Still a hole in this same block: line 94 (and the later Stack-Aware Path section). It reads as if stackPath works. It does not, for the parent-push reason we already found. That nit is not written into the doc yet.

The **hole** is: the doc talks as if `stackPath` works. In CARE today it does not, for a boring code reason.

**What `stackPath` is supposed to do**

“Only swap this component when it sits under that parent.”

```
condition: { stackPath: ["PatientHome", "PatientCard"] }
```

Meaning: override `PatientCard` only if React rendered it **inside** `PatientHome`.

**What the code actually does**

Each sleeve can take two roads:

```
no stackPath on this key  →  fast path  →  draw UI, do NOT write "I am PatientHome"
has stackPath on this key →  slow path  →  write "I am PatientCard" onto a parent list
```

The parent list is only updated on the **slow** road.

`PatientHome` almost never has its own `stackPath`, so it takes the fast road and **never writes its name**.

Then `PatientCard` looks at the list:

```
wanted:  PatientHome → PatientCard
actual:  (empty) → PatientCard     ← parent never signed in
```

Match fails. Override does not apply.

**What line 94 does wrong**

It says: if stack conditions exist → walk the tree and resolve. That sounds like a working feature. The walk only sees names that took the slow road. Parents usually did not.

Same family as `userRole`: the field exists; CARE does not fill the board the feature needs.

**Takeaway:** Line 94 is not a lie that the branch exists. It is a lie that a plugin author can use `stackPath` today and have parent matching work. That warning is not in the doc yet.

content.text:
Use the **conversation / composer ID**, not **Request ID**. Request ID is one model turn (for support). Import/resume needs the whole-chat ID.

**From the chat UI**

1. Open the chat you want.
2. Click **⋯** in the chat header.
3. **Copy ID** (or conversation ID) — that is the session.
4. Skip **Copy Request ID**.

**From Cursor CLI** (if that is the chat you mean)

```text
/copy-conversation-id
```

**From disk** (this workspace)

The filename is the ID:

```text
~/.cursor/projects/home-yaswanth-ohc-care/agent-transcripts/<uuid>.jsonl
```

This override/docs thread is `54c88f24-74f3-4354-97c6-7a86230f4538`.

---

**What “import” actually does**

| You have | You can |
|---|---|
| Share link `cursor.com/s/…` | Someone else **Fork to Cursor** (Teams/Enterprise) |
| Cloud agent `cursor.com/agents/bc-…` | Open on another machine |
| CLI chat ID | `agent --resume <id>` |
| Local UUID from ⋯ / `agent-transcripts` | Identifies the chat **on this machine**. It is not a paste-to-import token for another PC |

Local IDE chats do not sync by UUID. Same project on the same computer: search the Agents sidebar (`Ctrl/Cmd+K`) or `@Chats`. Another machine: Share/Fork or a Cloud Agent URL, not the local UUID.
